limitations: Nine affected individuals from eight families support recessive RFC4 disease through rare biallelic variants, segregation, RNA-splicing studies, patient fibroblast RFC4 abundance and complex assays. This is a discovery cohort, not independent clinical validation. Neurological tissue mechanism remains unmeasured; no vestibular testing, disease-relevant cell model or animal model (Discussion).

Figures4–6/S1–S4/S9–S11: protein abundance, complex formation and enzymatic activity differ. C-terminal antibodies target residues181–363 versus N-terminal1–50; altered epitopes can affect measured abundance. HeLa clones are hypertriploid edited lines with residual in-frame products, not clean diploid nulls. Clone2 third allele unidentified. RFC4 exon10–11 qPCR loss does not establish whole-transcript loss; upstream expression persists.

Figure5 patient fibroblasts1/2/4/5: RFC4 reduction varies by antibody and person; RFC1/RFC5/RAD17 mostly preserved in1/2 but depleted in4/5. Not uniform loss of all subunits in every person. Some blots/coIP are single experiments; quantified bands often technical replicates. Overexpression coIP does not by itself distinguish binding affinity from yield/abundance.

Figure6C/S10: purified complexes containing I327dup, E344K or C281R retain PCNA loading, without significant difference from WT; RFC1 ΔN554 used,12.5/25nM complexes and artificial gapped DNA. Purification of equal complex concentrations does not test cellular complex yield. These results limit blanket complete loss-of-function claims.

FigureS11: S-phase impairment is chiefly Individual1 (18h11.5% versus44.5% control), while Individual2 is27.4% versus27.5%; at20h22.3% versus42.7% and36.1% versus40.3%. Findings not universal cell-cycle arrest. Graphical abstract appropriately marks S-phase progression with question mark.

Figure1A Family8 reverses sexes: labelled Individual8 is drawn square and9 circle, whereas Table1 and case narratives identify8female/9male. Family8 siblings are not independent families. Both tested negative for familial DMD variant present in their brother.

Table3 gives RFC4 microcephaly absent, conflicting with Table1 positives4/5/8/9. Table3/S6 cognitive impairment absent conflicts with Individual6 narrative WAIS-III in70s and Individual2 minimally impaired cognition. TableS6 retains7-person denominators and2/7 cerebellar atrophy despite final9-person cohort and Table1 atrophy1/2/5/6; its dystonia-negative conflicts with Individual2, hyporeflexia-negative with absent reflexes in5. Do not use comparative summary as individual clinical truth.

FiguresS5/S6 reporting defects: S6 calls c.966+2dup while Table2/S5 and main use c.996+2dup. S5 caption mistakenly assigns c.996+2dup to Individual4 and c.1064_1065del to5; S5 panel labels and Table2 show the reverse case association. S1 primer table labels both c.290+5G>T primers F. Prefer explicit sequence panels/Table2 with caveats.

c.996+2dup causes multiple exon-skipping products, not one uniquely established protein change; intron9/10 retention and partial exon10 skipping also occur in controls. S5 caption says exon10 skipping most frequent, while Figure2 caption/Table2 mention combined exon9/10 commonly. Exact isoform proportions not established.

Additional candidate note/TableS7: Individual2 homozygous SCAF8 NM_001286188:c.167C>T p.A56V,GRCh37chr6:155054967C>T,frequency0.32822%(602),possible uncalled homozygote in gnomAD; no established Mendelian association. Individual5 SEMA4F H302N maternal/P620L paternal in trans, also unestablished. These remain possible contributions, not validated alternate diagnoses. Individual2 additionally CHEK2 I157T cancer-risk allele and maternal538kb21q22.12 duplication (case narrative).

Individual7 prematurity30+6weeks,IUGR,mild asphyxia and later cardiopulmonary arrest are phenotype confounders. Individual5 acquired bilateral posterior injury following status and later hypoxic encephalopathy should not be attributed automatically to RFC4 developmental malformation.

Genomic normalization from sourceGRCh37 to packetGRCh38 was not independently recalculated. Coding HGVS/transcript NM_002916.5 and zygosity checked exactly; differing normalized genomic coordinates are explicitly unresolved, not silently treated as same-build matches. Raw sequencing/flow files not reanalyzed.
